incidents.title: Overhead line incident at Montmelian
incidents.description: Loss of voltage on track 1. Traffic suspended between Montmelian and Pontcharra. Territorial crisis room opened. No injuries reported.
incidents.summary:
**Summary — INC-2026-041 · Overhead line incident at Montmelian (G3, in progress)**

Contact wire rupture confirmed at KM 12.8 on track 1, between Montmelian and Pontcharra. Traffic suspended on this track; track 2 remains in operation under regulation. **Confirmed assessment**: 1,850 passengers affected, 12 trains affected including 3 cancelled, delays estimated at 45–90 min. Four teams mobilized for wire replacement. Passenger information issued, water distribution at stations, adapted transport plan in force. **Progressive recovery estimated at 12:25 UTC**, subject to on-site technical validation. No injuries reported.

five_whys.question: Why was a track interrupted?
five_whys.answer: The contact wire rupture prevented a safe power supply to the trains.

five_whys.question: Why did the contact wire rupture?
five_whys.answer: Localized wear near a suspension point had reduced its effective cross-section.

five_whys.question: Why was this wear not addressed before the rupture?
five_whys.answer: The last visual inspection did not include a precise measurement at this singular point.

five_whys.question: Why was this point not subject to a targeted measurement?
five_whys.answer: The inspection program followed a uniform periodicity despite higher local stress.

five_whys.question: Why did the program remain uniform?
five_whys.answer: Field observations were not integrated into a prioritization of sensitive points.

action_items.title: Measure wear at neighboring suspension points
Adapt the overhead line patrol to sensitive points
Test the passenger plan in operation on a single track

five_whys.question: Why was voltage lost?
five_whys.answer: A degraded connection interrupted the power supply to the sector.

five_whys.question: Why did this connection degrade?
five_whys.answer: Insufficient tightening had caused progressive heating.

five_whys.question: Why was the insufficient tightening not detected?

five_whys.question: Why was the sector closed?
five_whys.answer: A broken support had misaligned the contact wire and made current collection dangerous.

five_whys.question: Why did the support break?
five_whys.answer: Internal corrosion had weakened its fastening.

five_whys.question: Why was the corrosion not spotted?
five_whys.answer: The area masked by the fastening was not visible during routine patrols.

five_whys.question: Why was no additional inspection scheduled?

five_whys.question: Why was this at-risk family not identified?
five_whys.answer: The equipment inventory did not link the support series to defects observed elsewhere.

five_whys.question: Why did the zone remain occupied?
five_whys.answer: A faulty connection prevented the detection from returning to the clear state.

five_whys.question: Why was the connection faulty?
